realDryRun.notes: Real BSC -> Sui Testnet transfer through a brand-new native Move contract (sui/programs/inaya_bridge_sui), NOT Wormhole -- same reasoning as Aptos's native bridge (see deployments/bridge/aptosTestnet.json). Validators are tracked by their 33-byte COMPRESSED secp256k1 public key (what sui::ecdsa_k1::secp256k1_ecrecover actually returns), not an Ethereum-style address -- no reason to reconstruct that EVM-specific derivation on Sui. A real bug WAS found and fixed here (unlike Aptos, which worked first try): the first attempt's off-chain relayer script built each signature's recovery-id byte via `ethers.toBeArray(yParity)`, which returns a ZERO-LENGTH array when yParity is 0 (minimal big-endian encoding of the value 0 has no bytes) -- silently truncating the signature from 65 to 64 bytes and making Sui's ecdsa_k1::secp256k1_ecrecover abort with EInvalidSignature. Root-caused by comparing the failed transaction's actual on-chain BCS-decoded arguments (`sui client tx-block <digest>`) against isolated Move unit tests proving the message-hash and signature-recovery logic were both already correct -- fixed by using `Uint8Array.of(yParity)` instead, which always emits exactly one byte. The on-chain Move contract itself needed zero changes.
